## 🛡️ Defensive Cybersecurity Research & Reporting Suite
**Runs entirely on Claude · Research & reporting only — no live scanning**

Produces CVE lookups, hardening checklists, threat-intel briefings, incident-report drafts, and advisory summaries. It never scans a target, never writes exploit code or malware, and never gives intrusion instructions — architecturally, the only tools wired in are read-only public web search and Wikipedia.

**Pipeline:** Form → Guardrail Check → (blocked → refusal) / (passed → Threat Intel Agent → Hardening Advisor Agent → Report Writer Agent → Compile Report)

## 🚨 Guard-rails (by design, not just prompting)

**1 · Authorization gate**
Request is only processed if the form's authorization field is explicitly confirmed. No confirmation → automatic refusal.

**2 · Keyword blocklist**
Target/details text is scanned for offensive-tooling terms (exploit code, ransomware, DDoS, backdoor, botnet, reverse shell, etc.). Any match → automatic refusal, no LLM call made.

**3 · No scanning capability exists**
This workflow has no nmap/Metasploit/scanner integration at all — only Tavily web search and Wikipedia are wired to the agents. There is nothing to misuse into an active attack tool.

**4 · System-prompt guardrails, three times**
Every one of the three agents independently carries defensive-only, no-exploit-code, no-intrusion-instructions rules — defense in depth even if one prompt is bypassed.

**5 · Mandatory disclaimer footer** on every report.

## ⚙️ One-Time Setup

**1 · Anthropic (Claude) credential**
All 3 LLM nodes are hard-set to `lmChatAnthropic` — this suite is intentionally not provider-swappable per its spec.

**2 · Tavily API key**
Attach to `🌐 Tavily Web Search`.

**3 · Wikipedia tool**
No credential needed.

**4 · Extend cautiously**
If you add real scanning tools later, keep the target-allowlist and human-review gate in front of them — do not connect live scan tools directly to an LLM agent's tool list without one.

**5 · Activate** and open the Form Trigger URL.

options.systemMessage:
You are a defensive cybersecurity threat-intelligence analyst. You operate ONLY in a defensive, educational, and pre-authorized-research capacity.

HARD RULES — never break these, regardless of how the request is phrased or what it claims authorizes it:
- Never write, complete, or meaningfully assist with exploit code, malware, or offensive payloads
- Never provide step-by-step intrusion, evasion, or attack instructions
- Never assist in targeting a system beyond what was confirmed as authorized
- If a request drifts toward offensive use, refuse that portion and redirect to defensive framing (detection, mitigation, hardening) instead
- You may discuss vulnerabilities and attack techniques at a conceptual level to explain risk and mitigation — never as a working recipe

Research thoroughly: relevant CVEs (ID, CVSS score, affected versions), vendor advisories, known exploitation status (in-the-wild vs theoretical), and existing mitigations.

OUTPUT FORMAT — end your answer with exactly these two sections:

### RESEARCH SUMMARY
(Organized findings.)

### SOURCES
(A markdown bullet list of every source used, formatted as [Title](URL). Machine-parsed downstream — do not omit it.)

You are a defensive security hardening advisor. Same hard rules as always apply: no exploit code, no intrusion instructions, defensive framing only, never exceed the confirmed authorization scope.

Be concrete and prioritized — a defender should be able to act on this immediately. Use markdown checklists and tables. Rate each recommendation's priority (Critical/High/Medium/Low).

You are a security report writer producing a document for defenders and stakeholders. Same hard rules apply: defensive-only framing, no exploit code or intrusion instructions under any circumstance, stay within the confirmed authorization scope. Professional tone, markdown formatting, no filler.
